Product Strategy Proposal • Concept Case Study

Book the night.
Know the ride.

Making every concert journey seamless, from booking tickets to getting home.

District Rides is a proposed integrated mobility experience for District by Zomato that allows concert-goers to reserve fixed-fare transportation while purchasing their event tickets. By connecting ticketing and mobility, District Rides aims to eliminate the uncertainty of finding a cab after late-night concerts.

01 / EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

An experience doesn't end when the concert ends.

District has built an experience around discovering and booking entertainment, including concerts, events, movies, dining and live experiences.

However, one important part of attending a late-night event remains outside the booking experience: transportation.

For concert-goers who depend on app-based mobility services, returning home after a popular event can become difficult due to surge pricing, limited vehicle availability and long waiting times.

District Rides proposes an integrated transportation service that allows users to book a ride alongside their concert tickets. Users can choose between return-only and round-trip transportation, see a fixed fare upfront and reserve vehicle capacity before the event.

The proposed service uses a hybrid fleet model consisting of established mobility partners and verified independent drivers. The commercial model is based on negotiated partner pricing, allowing customers to receive a discounted fare while District retains a gross contribution on completed journeys.

The larger objective is to extend District's value proposition beyond booking an experience to making the entire experience easier to attend.
Strategic Architecture

Core Pillar Summary

  • 01
    Point-of-Commitment Integration Offered as an optional checkout add-on when intent and event details are already locked in.
  • 02
    Asset-Light Hybrid Supply Orchestrates established mobility providers and verified independent fleet operators without owning vehicles.
  • 03
    Non-Subsidised Discounted Fixed Fare Negotiates bulk advance partner rates (e.g. ₹600 illustrative) to offer users ₹680 vs ₹800 peak surge while retaining ₹80 gross contribution.
  • 04
    Replacement-First Reliability Prioritises automatic replacement vehicle allocation over bare refunds if an assigned driver cancels.
02 / PROBLEM DISCOVERY

The night ends. The uncertainty begins.

District lists numerous concerts and live events, many of which finish around 11:00 PM or later. At the end of a popular concert, hundreds or thousands of attendees try to book cabs simultaneously—creating concentrated demand around a single location where most attendees depend on services such as Uber and Ola.

Problem 01 • Surge Pricing ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE

Dramatic post-event fare spikes

Normal transportation costs can increase dramatically after an event. A journey that would ordinarily cost ₹400 could cost approximately ₹800 during peak post-event demand.

Normal Reference Journey ₹400
Illustrative Peak-Demand Fare ₹800 (+100% Increase)
Price Shock Multiplier 2.0x (+100% surge)

*Note: ₹400 and ₹800 are illustrative examples demonstrating concentrated post-event surge mechanics rather than verified market averages.

Problem 02

Difficulty finding available cabs

Users may spend 30–45 minutes attempting to find an available vehicle after the concert due to:

  • • Large crowds requesting simultaneously
  • • Limited supply around the venue
  • • Severe traffic congestion
  • • Drivers avoiding difficult pickup locations
  • • High demand in a short time window
Problem 03

Uncertainty about returning home

Users know exactly when and where the concert is happening when they buy tickets weeks in advance, but they cannot confidently plan their return transportation.

Creates persistent late-night anxiety that detracts from enjoying the final encore of the live event.

Problem 04

Outbound venue travel is also costly

The problem is not restricted to returning home. When thousands travel towards a popular venue simultaneously, ride prices increase before the event too.

Attendees who only want to catch the main act also prefer choosing a specific arrival window rather than travelling with the first gate-opening crowd.

Problem 05

People living away from hometowns

Young professionals who relocate to metropolitan cities for employment often do not own personal vehicles.

With late-night public transit limited or inconvenient, app-based cabs and two-wheelers are their primary lifeline—making reliable mobility essential.

Defined Problem Statement

"Concert-goers can book their event tickets in advance, but they cannot confidently plan their journey home. Last-minute transportation after late-night concerts often involves unpredictable fares, limited cab availability and long waiting times."

Core Product Insight
"Users are not just looking for a cheaper cab. They are looking for certainty."

04 / PROPOSED SOLUTION & OPERATING MODEL

Meet District Rides.

District Rides is an integrated mobility service that allows users to pre-book transportation while purchasing concert tickets. The service provides fixed-fare, scheduled pickup and drop transportation for attendees.

OPTION A • PRIMARY USE CASE

Return-Only

The user books a vehicle to pick them up from the concert venue after the event and drop them at their destination.

Solves the #1 user pain point: post-concert return uncertainty.
OPTION B • COMPLETE JOURNEY

Round-Trip

Books both a ride from their chosen pickup location to the venue (at their preferred arrival time) and a return ride scheduled around the event's expected end time.

Ideal for users timing arrival for the main act.
OPTION C • ZERO FRICTION

No Cab Required

The user can skip the transportation add-on and proceed with normal concert ticket checkout immediately.

Guardrail: Never make District Rides mandatory.

Independent Passenger Count Rule

OPERATIONAL ARCHITECTURE

Driver & Fleet Operating Model

District does not need to own a vehicle fleet. Instead, District acts as the orchestration and booking layer connecting event demand with hybrid mobility supply.

01 • Supply Architecture

Hybrid Fleet Model

Combines two complementary supply pools under District's orchestration layer:

1. Established Mobility Providers Fleet APIs and negotiated event blocks with large ride-sharing or rental operators.
2. Verified Independent Drivers & Local Fleets Pre-vetted local operators contracted for high-density event dispersal windows.
02 • Dispatch & Buffer Rule

Driver Scheduling Mechanism

  • • Drivers receive bookings and scheduled pickup windows in advance.
  • • Drivers may complete other trips beforehand, provided they remain available for the committed concert pickup window.
  • PROPOSED DRIVER-ARRIVAL RULE: Driver must arrive at the designated concert pickup zone ~15 minutes before the scheduled event end time (proposed operational rule, not yet a validated standard).
  • • Drivers are compensated for reservation commitments and waiting time.
  • • Event delays trigger dynamic pickup schedule adjustments.
03 • Failover Protocol

Replacement Cancellation Policy

A refund alone at 11:30 PM outside a stadium does not solve the customer's immediate problem. Our policy is Replacement Allocation:

  1. 1. Assigned driver cancels → District triggers instant replacement request.
  2. 2. System checks eligible standby partner capacity in the venue zone.
  3. 3. Replacement vehicle is assigned & customer gets updated details.
  4. 4. If no replacement is available → Escalation & priority service recovery.

07 / BUSINESS MODEL & UNIT STRUCTURE

Creating value for customers, partners and District.

District operates as a mobility orchestration platform. The primary revenue model is based on negotiated partner pricing: District negotiates a partner payout for an event-linked ride and charges the customer a slightly higher amount while maintaining a discount against the illustrative reference market fare.

ILLUSTRATIVE UNIT ECONOMICS WATERFALL PER COMPLETED RIDE
1. Illustrative Reference Market Fare (Post-Event Peak) ₹800
100% Reference Benchmark
2. District Rides Fixed Customer Fare (15% Saving) ₹680 (Saves ₹120)
Customer Pays ₹680
-₹120
3. Negotiated Mobility Partner Payout ₹600
Partner Payout ₹600
+₹80
Exact Unit Calculations (Illustrative Assumptions):
District Gross Contribution: ₹680 − ₹600 = ₹80
Customer Saving vs Reference: ₹800 − ₹680 = ₹120
Customer Discount Percentage: ₹120 / ₹800 = 15%
District Gross Contribution Margin: ₹80 / ₹680 = 11.76%

*All figures are illustrative unit assumptions designed to test commercial logic.

Crucial Distinction #1 • Discount ≠ Subsidy

Why the ₹120 customer saving is not a cash subsidy

The proposed model does not assume District directly pays the ₹120 discount out of pocket. Instead, the discount comes from negotiating a lower partner payout (₹600) relative to the ₹800 peak reference fare by giving fleet partners guaranteed advance demand visibility.

The negotiated ₹600 partner payout is assumed to include agreed driver compensation and operational responsibilities (including advance reservation, availability commitment, and the 15-minute waiting buffer), which may still be higher than a normal ₹400 off-peak ride.

Crucial Distinction #2 • Gross Contribution ≠ Net Profit

What the ₹80 Gross Contribution excludes

The ₹80 per completed ride is strictly gross contribution before operating expenses. It does not deduct:

• Payment gateway charges
• Customer support ops
• Refunds & cancellations
• Service recovery costs
• Tech & API integration
• Marketing & taxes
MONETISATION EXPANSION (UNVALIDATED HYPOTHESES)

Four Potential Revenue Streams

Initial launch remains strictly focused on Concerts
01 • PRIMARY

Partner Margin

The primary proposed model. District retains the spread between the fixed customer fare and the negotiated partner payout.

02 • B2B SUPPLY

Mobility Commissions

Negotiate structured referral or fulfilment commissions with established citywide mobility partners for high-value event traffic.

03 • SPONSORSHIP

Event Organiser Partnerships

Event organisers may co-sponsor transportation offers to boost ticket conversion, improve attendance, and reduce venue exit congestion.

04 • LONG-TERM

Category Cross-Selling

Future expansion into large live experiences, sporting events, late-night entertainment, and selected special dining experiences.

COMMERCIAL DEPENDENCY

Partner economics are the #1 commercial lever

If mobility partner payouts increase due to tight late-night supply or waiting-time compensation demands, District must respond through four strategic levers:

  • 01 Negotiate better bulk rates by guaranteeing high-density demand corridors for event nights.
  • 02 Adjust customer fixed pricing dynamically while preserving pickup certainty.
  • 03 Obtain event organiser sponsorship to subsidise venue dispersal capacity.
  • 04 Accept lower contribution margins temporarily during initial pilot validation without making the unit economics structurally negative.
09 / PRODUCT STRATEGY, MVP & ROADMAP

Start narrow. Prove the experience. Scale intelligently.

Initial Target Segment: Large concerts expected to finish after 10:00 PM. Rather than building a general cab-booking marketplace, the MVP focuses strictly on solving late-night concert dispersal.

STRATEGIC ROLLOUT

Three-Phase Product Roadmap

PHASE 01 • MVP & VALIDATION

Prove Core Concert Reliability

  • • Launch for selected large concerts (>10 PM finish).
  • • Return-only and round-trip booking options.
  • • Upfront discounted fixed fares.
  • • Hybrid partner supply integration.
  • • Automatic driver replacement protocol.
  • • Real-time notifications and customer support.
  • • Measure fulfilment reliability and adoption.
PHASE 02 • EXPERIENCE EXPANSION

Deepen Group & Timing Flexibility

  • • Multiple drop-off locations for friend groups.
  • • On-demand early return requests.
  • • Automated event-delay schedule syncing.
  • • Expanded vehicle category selection.
  • • In-app group ride coordination tools.
PHASE 03 • SCALE & OPTIMISATION

Multi-Category & Network Scale

  • • Expand into sports & live entertainment categories.
  • • Predictive spatial demand forecasting.
  • • Deeper regional mobility partnerships.
  • • High-capacity shared event shuttles.
  • • Co-sponsored event organiser partnerships.
  • • Bi-directional fleet utilisation optimisation.

VALIDATION & A/B TESTING PROTOCOL

Controlled Checkout Experiment & Discovery Plan

Suggested Pilot Period: 4–6 Weeks
Control Group (50%)

Standard Ticket Checkout

Eligible users see the existing concert ticket-booking experience without the District Rides add-on. Establishes baseline ticket checkout conversion.

Test Group (50%)

Integrated District Rides Add-On

Eligible users see the optional District Rides add-on (Return-only / Round-trip / No cab required) during ticket checkout.

Experiment Objective & Guardrail: Determine whether integrated mobility increases user satisfaction and generates sustainable commercial contribution without negatively affecting core concert ticket checkout conversion.
5-Step Pre-Launch & Pilot Validation Plan
  1. 01. 10–15 qualitative interviews with recent late-night concert attendees.
  2. 02. Clickable prototype usability test of the 6-screen checkout and pickup flow.
  3. 03. Mobility partner discovery to validate ₹600 payout feasibility and SLA buffers.
  4. 04. Pricing willingness-to-pay validation across solo and group ticket buyers.
  5. 05. Small live pilot (4–6 weeks) across selected high-attendance concerts.
OPERATIONAL & COMMERCIAL RESILIENCE

Risk Analysis & Mitigation Matrix

FINAL CONCLUSION • PRODUCT SYNTHESIS

Make getting home part of the experience.

District Rides extends District's value proposition beyond discovering and booking entertainment experiences. It addresses a meaningful transportation problem faced by concert-goers who depend on app-based mobility services.

By integrating fixed-fare transportation into the ticket-booking experience, District can help customers plan their complete concert journey while creating a new mobility revenue opportunity.

The Proposal Combines Seven Core Disciplines:
01. User-centric problem solving 02. Integrated product design 03. Hybrid mobility supply 04. Predictable pricing 05. Partner economics 06. Operational reliability 07. Incremental monetisation
"Booking a concert should also mean having a reliable way to get home."
